statement: Table 1 defines 0R as no rejection, 1R as mild, 2R as moderate, and 3R as severe acute cellular rejection, with increasingly extensive infiltrates and myocyte damage.
supports: Use the revised ISHLT grades as the source vocabulary before any task-specific label collapse.
does_not_establish: It does not validate a particular binary cutoff, loss function, or clinical decision threshold.
method_or_result: ISHLT multidisciplinary consensus revision approved in 2004 and published in 2005.

statement: The pAMR table distinguishes negative, histopathology-only, immunopathology-only, combined, and severe pathological AMR categories.
supports: AMR target definitions must record which histologic and immunopathologic inputs are actually available.
does_not_establish: An H&E-only model cannot be described as reproducing complete pAMR categorization without the missing immunopathology evidence.
method_or_result: AHA scientific statement endorsed by ISHLT, Table 5.

source_locator.section: Table 5: Proposed Nomenclature for Pathological AMR

statement: CRANE was developed on US data and evaluated on independent cohorts from Turkey and Switzerland, reporting AUCs for rejection detection, ACR, AMR, Quilty B lesions, and rejection grade.
supports: Cardiac allograft WSI modeling is technically feasible and can be evaluated across institutions and scanning pipelines.
does_not_establish: The results do not guarantee transportability to SMC data, local stains, magnification, scanners, or endpoints.
method_or_result: Retrospective multicenter development, independent international testing, and reader comparison.

statement: An attention-based model using self-supervised features was trained on a primary cardiac transplant cohort and deployed to three additional cohorts.
supports: A second independent study supports feasibility of weakly supervised rejection detection from routine cardiac pathology slides.
does_not_establish: Feasibility does not imply adequate clinical utility or local-domain validity.
method_or_result: 1,079 slides from 325 patients across three German transplant centers.

statement: Binary AUROC was 0.849 in primary-cohort cross-validation and 0.734, 0.729, and 0.716 in three external validation cohorts.
supports: Independent-cohort results can be materially lower than internal cross-validation and should be reported separately.
does_not_establish: This single study does not quantify the expected performance drop for the SMC cohort or identify its cause.
method_or_result: Cross-validation followed by frozen-model deployment to three cohorts.

statement: CACHE-Grader used 154 handcrafted histologic features on 2,472 slides and was evaluated for cellular rejection grading; its limitations state that it is not designed for AMR-related features or future rejection risk.
supports: A biologically motivated non-foundation-model comparator is appropriate for ACR grading.
does_not_establish: Its evidence cannot be transferred to AMR or prognostic event prediction.
method_or_result: Three-center multicenter validation with pathologist comparisons and an explicit limitations analysis.

statement: The study analyzed longitudinal rejection biology in 62 recipients using selected 0.6 mm tissue-microarray cores, a 477-gene Xenium panel, and registered H&E images; 195 of 233 targeted cores were retained.
supports: GSE290577 is relevant for molecular and longitudinal biological analysis of rejection.
does_not_establish: Selected tissue cores are not an independent routine-WSI screening cohort and should not be counted as external WSI validation.
method_or_result: Preprint using targeted spatial transcriptomics on tissue microarrays with image registration.

source_locator.section: Abstract; Tissue microarray construction and Xenium workflow

statement: CLAM uses slide labels, attention pooling, and instance-level clustering to classify WSIs and generate attention heatmaps.
supports: CLAM is an appropriate weakly supervised WSI baseline when only slide- or event-level labels are available.
does_not_establish: The original non-cardiac benchmarks do not prove local cardiac performance, and attention heatmaps are not validated causal explanations.
method_or_result: General-purpose WSI MIL method evaluated on multiple computational pathology tasks.

statement: UNI was pretrained on more than 100 million H&E tissue patches from more than 100,000 diagnostic WSIs across 20 major tissue types; slide tasks first extract patch embeddings and then aggregate them.
supports: UNI is a strong general-purpose candidate for patch-level feature extraction.
does_not_establish: Pretraining scale does not establish superiority for cardiac allograft biopsies, non-H&E stains, a chosen magnification, or event-level aggregation.
method_or_result: Large-scale self-supervised pathology pretraining with ROI- and slide-level downstream evaluation.

statement: ABMIL defines a trainable neural attention operator that is permutation invariant and yields instance contribution weights for bag prediction.
supports: It supplies a principled baseline for unordered patch-to-slide or slide-to-event aggregation.
does_not_establish: Attention weights are not automatically faithful, causal, or clinically calibrated explanations.
method_or_result: MIL formulation derived from symmetric aggregation and evaluated on benchmark datasets.

statement: TransMIL uses a Transformer-based correlated-MIL framework to model morphological, spatial, and pairwise instance information.
supports: It is a reasonable contextual-MIL comparator when inter-patch relationships may matter.
does_not_establish: Cancer-benchmark gains do not establish superiority on small cardiac allograft cohorts or event-level bags.
method_or_result: NeurIPS architecture study on CAMELYON16 and TCGA cancer tasks.

statement: Across H&E data from four organs and nine laboratories, the study compared stain color augmentation and normalization as ways to reduce cross-laboratory generalization error.
supports: Stain and site shift should be measured and mitigation strategies should be ablated.
does_not_establish: The tested H&E patch/CNN settings do not determine the best policy for every stain, encoder, or event-level architecture.
method_or_result: Multi-organ, multi-laboratory experimental comparison of stain interventions.

statement: TRIPOD+AI supplies 27 main reporting items and 52 subitems spanning model development and evaluation, including data, fairness, open science, performance, limitations, and generalizability.
supports: Use TRIPOD+AI as the reporting checklist for this clinical prediction-model research.
does_not_establish: Complete reporting does not prove low bias, external validity, or clinical benefit.
method_or_result: International guideline-development process and expanded checklist.

statement: PROBAST+AI separates model development from model evaluation and assesses four domains using 16 development and 18 evaluation signaling questions.
supports: Use PROBAST+AI to assess development quality, evaluation risk of bias, and applicability.
does_not_establish: It is not a reporting guideline and cannot replace independent performance evaluation.

statement: TRIPOD+AI asks authors to identify differences between development and evaluation data and report heterogeneity in performance across clusters when examined.
supports: Patient and center grouping, repeated observations, and cluster-specific performance should be explicit in the study report.
does_not_establish: The checklist does not prescribe the exact split algorithm for this dataset.
method_or_result: Checklist items on training versus evaluation and model performance across clusters.

statement: The PROBAST+AI evaluation analysis domain explicitly asks whether data leakage was avoided when splitting training and test datasets and whether resampling replicated all model-development steps.
supports: Patient-level separation and fully nested preprocessing/resampling are risk-of-bias controls for repeated-biopsy data.
does_not_establish: The tool does not identify a single universally correct resampling scheme for the local cohort.
